_meta.description: Declarative rule catalog for the planning engine. One entry per rule R1–R8. tier = priority (1 = highest; lower tiers never override higher). params are read by the engine; do not hardcode thresholds elsewhere. Every active rule MUST carry source + evidenceLevel (enforced by test T11). evidenceLevel scale: meta-analysis > rct > cohort > expert-consensus > assumption.
_meta.swapNote: swap = exercise-level adjustment (spec v2.0 §3.4): affected exercises (load >= 2 on trigger region) are exchanged/removed, timing and remaining volume stay. Allowed on FIXED sessions — fixed protects timing, not content. Hollow-out guard: if drop > keep, fall back to move/reduce. Dedupe rank: swap 0 < reduce 1 < move 2 < remove 3.
_meta.note: R8 is a generator rule (split coverage), not an in-week replanning trigger.

rules.name: Pain-Monitoring Model
rules.logic: NRS <= 2: no action. Strength sessions: exercise level first — swapProposal exchanges the exercises loading the painful region >= 2 (both NRS 3–5 and NRS > 5); if the hollow-out guard triggers (majority affected), fall back: NRS 3–5 -> reduce the session; NRS > 5 -> remove (non-fixed) or strongly reduce (fixed). Additional condition: pain the following day must not exceed baseline. Fixed units are never moved/removed.

source.citation: Silbernagel KG, Thomeé R, Eriksson BI, Karlsson J. Continued Sports Activity, Using a Pain-Monitoring Model, During Rehabilitation in Patients With Achilles Tendinopathy: A Randomized Controlled Study. Am J Sports Med. 2007;35(6):897–906.

rules.evidenceNote: Level 1 (randomized). Original model validated on the Achilles tendon (pain <=5/10 during activity, not markedly increasing afterward, returning to baseline next day). Application to other structures is common clinical practice but extrapolated — flagged, not presented as validated per-structure.

rules.name: Permanent Constraints
rules.logic: Per profile constraint: yellow -> replace matching exercises with an alternative (e.g. avoid kneeFlexionTag 'deep' under a knee_flexion constraint, use 'low'/'mid'). red -> do not load the region at all. Applied both in replanning and in the generator's exercise selection.

source.citation: User-defined constraint. Substitution/exclusion mechanic follows standard load-management practice; constraint content is a user preference, not a literature claim.

rules.evidenceNote: Mechanism is expert-consensus; the specific constraint (e.g. knee flexion 80–90 deg under load) is a user-provided input, not derived from a study.

rules.name: Tendon/Pulley Recovery
rules.logic: After a session flagged tendonHeavy AND hardFingerLoad, the fingers region carries an extended recovery constant. Until recovered, do not propose a second high finger load (boulder limit session or high-grip strength pull) -> reduce/move. V1 rule of thumb: >= 48 h between two high finger loads. Without the hardFingerLoad flag, R3 falls back to the static boulder profile and is marked lower-confidence.

source.citation: Low S. Rehabbing injured pulleys — loading frequency ~3x/week or every other day to allow tissue recovery. Supplemental practitioner sources: The Climbing Doctor (pulley rehab); Hooper's Beta A2 Pulley Manual.

rules.evidenceNote: No validated study exists on the recovery duration of a HEALTHY pulley between training stimuli. The 48 h value is a conservative practitioner heuristic and is explicitly low-evidence. Pulley overload is often not felt as fatigue before becoming symptomatic — hence the hardFingerLoad flag is the only reliable input.

rules.name: Eccentric Fatigue / DOMS (post-mountain)
rules.logic: After a session flagged eccentric (mainly mountain-day descent), affected regions (quads, posterior_chain, calves) carry a 24–72 h recovery window with peak soreness 24–72 h. Strength session within the window: swapProposal first (only leg loaders >= 2 exchanged, rest stays — typical full-body case); if the hollow-out guard triggers (pure leg session): move (non-fixed, typically 48–72 h spacing) or reduce (fixed). Window scales with elevation gain.

source.citation: DOMS/EIMD time course (peak 24–72 h, resolves ~5–7 d): Physiopedia, Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness; ScienceDirect, 'Eccentric exercise: muscle damage to the new normal' (2026). Downhill running as the classic eccentric-EIMD model: Eston et al. (1995), as commonly cited.

rules.evidenceNote: DOMS time course is well established (cohort/review level). The elevation-gain scaling is an assumption. The repeated-bout effect (habituated athletes show attenuated DOMS) is NOT modeled in V1 — the full window is applied conservatively; flagged as assumption. Self-corrects via the feedback loop (V2).

rules.name: General Muscular Recovery
rules.logic: Regions at müde (yellow) -> reduced reloading for 24–48 h; platt (red) -> >= 48–72 h, no heavy reloading. Strength sessions: swapProposal on the region first (also on fixed sessions — fixed protects timing, not content); fallback: platt -> move, müde -> reduce. Combines the fatigue traffic-light input with regional load from §3.1.

source.citation: General training physiology: muscle protein synthesis window and DOMS recovery course (see R4 references).

rules.evidenceNote: Consensus-level heuristic combining subjective regional fatigue with modeled regional load.

rules.name: Strength/Endurance Interference
rules.logic: (a) Strength + endurance same day: if times present, aim for >= 6 h apart; otherwise slot-separate. (b) Prefer strength before endurance when both unavoidable in one day (benefit mainly for lower-body dynamic strength). (c) High leg-endurance frequency together with heavy leg strength -> interference hint.

source.citation: Hickson RC (1980), Eur J Appl Physiol 45:255–263 — original interference finding. Schumann M, Feuerbacher JF, Sünkeler M, et al. Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Sports Med. 2022;52(3):601–612 (43 studies) — interference on maximal strength/hypertrophy is small; explosive strength slightly reduced, mainly in same-session concurrent work. 'The Role of Intra-Session Exercise Sequence in the Interference Effect: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis' (Sports Medicine) — resistance-before-endurance mildly favours lower-body dynamic strength over >= 5 weeks.

rules.evidenceNote: Meta-analytic evidence, but the interference effect is WEAKER than historically assumed — hence low priority (tier 5). For goal 'sport_support' it is largely non-critical; the rule mainly informs sensible slot ordering. The enduranceHighFreqThreshold is a tunable expert-consensus parameter, not a cited single value.

rules.name: ACWR Weekly Load Steering (systemic only in V1)
rules.logic: ACWR = acute load (7-day sum of sRPE-TL) / chronic load (28-day weekly average). Zones: <0.8 detraining; 0.8–1.3 sweet spot; 1.3–1.5 elevated; >1.5 warning. If projected weekend ACWR > 1.5: propose reducing/removing a NON-FIXED add-on load (typically running). V1: systemic axis only (validated Foster basis). No leg-axis ACWR (would multiply assumption-level decomposition by a contested metric); leg steering handled by R4/R5.

source.citation: Gabbett TJ. The training–injury prevention paradox: should athletes be training smarter and harder? Br J Sports Med. 2016;50(5):273–280. IOC consensus (2016) endorsed ACWR monitoring.

rules.evidenceNote: Documented criticism: mathematical coupling (Lolli et al. 2019) and sensitivity issues (Impellizzeri et al. 2020). Hence lowest priority. V1 uses the simple rolling-average variant; EWMA/REDI are documented V2 alternatives. Show this criticism openly in the rulebook screen.

rules.name: Split Coverage Check (generator)
rules.logic: When a split unit is disabled (e.g. Pull), check which regions become uncovered vs. covered by other sports. Bouldering covers upper_back/forearm/fingers well, but horizontal pulling and rear shoulder only weakly -> hint: 'gap: rear shoulder / horizontal pull — add 1–2 exercises into Push?' with concrete suggestions the V1 catalog can actually deliver.

source.citation: Climbing shoulder-prevention practice (antagonist training, rotator cuff / scapular balance).

rules.evidenceNote: Consensus-level; the suggested fixes are constrained to equipment available in V1 (dumbbell/band, no cable) so the hint is actionable.
